title: Agentic routing and delegated work
claim: Designed and runs a personal agentic workflow system that routes work to specialist modes and delegates jobs.
evidence: Working personal system in daily use; routing and delegated jobs are part of the live workflow.
boundary: Personal-scale system; do not claim enterprise infrastructure or model-training ownership.

title: Persistent context across sessions
claim: Designed workflow behavior that preserves context across sessions and delegated tasks.
evidence: Persistent context is part of the operating system used in practice.
boundary: Persistent context is real, but this is only adjacent evidence for retrieval/RAG and must go through human review.

title: Fallback and safe failure
claim: Designed fallback paths for delegated steps when execution fails.
evidence: Fallback behavior is part of the live personal workflow.
boundary: Shows product/orchestration judgment, not fault-tolerant infrastructure at enterprise scale.

title: Human confirmation for higher-risk actions
claim: Requires explicit human confirmation before higher-risk actions execute.
evidence: Human-confirmation gate is part of the live workflow behavior.
boundary: Do not imply every action is risk-scored by a formal production policy engine.

title: Three-field decision contract
claim: Reduced workflow decision logic to a reusable three-field contract: what happened, what next, who decides.
evidence: Public GitHub reference implementation with schema, demo, tests and integrations.
boundary: Reference pattern; not a workflow engine or policy runtime.

title: Executable system/person boundary
claim: Implemented a small executable policy for deciding when software may act and when a person should decide.
evidence: Reference JS implementation plus zero-dependency tests.
boundary: Tiny reference implementation, not validated policy science.

title: LangGraph and n8n integration mapping
claim: Mapped the same decision primitive to agent and workflow orchestration contexts without coupling the contract to one runtime.
evidence: Public integration examples for LangGraph interrupt-style human review and n8n branching.

title: Explainable fit-and-proof product architecture
claim: Designed a product workflow that starts with role-fit diagnosis and proof quality rather than generic CV rewriting.
evidence: Canonical product README and startup form packs define vacancy fit, missing-proof detection, proof-pack creation, interview defense and tracking.
boundary: Early validation; do not claim scaled product traction.

title: Honest non-fit decision rule
claim: Defined a product requirement that the system must be able to say do not apply instead of maximizing application volume.
evidence: Canonical product rules explicitly require honest non-fit warnings and explainable fit.
boundary: Product principle; business value still needs pilot validation.

title: Evidence graph / proof object model
claim: Modeled reusable evidence objects including role, proof, metric, story, objection, gap, asset and package.
evidence: Canonical product architecture lists these as reusable internal objects and shared infrastructure.
boundary: Product data model; not a production knowledge graph.

title: Concierge-first validation strategy
claim: Chose paid manual audits and proof packs before a heavy software build to validate willingness to pay and workflow value.
evidence: Launch mode explicitly prioritizes concierge-first, service revenue before software, and paid audits.
boundary: Validation strategy, not confirmed paid traction.

title: Before/after pilot measurement design
claim: Defined a pilot protocol around reply rate, interview rate, time-to-apply, willingness to pay and proof gaps.
evidence: Pilot tracker and candidate-case protocol specify baseline and after measures plus paid-pilot signals.
boundary: Metrics framework exists; uplift is not yet measured.

title: Human review for ambiguous proof
claim: Routes weak or ambiguous evidence to explicit human review instead of silently upgrading it into stronger proof.
evidence: Public v0.2 workflow has verified / needs_review / missing states and blocks unverified evidence from proof packs.
boundary: Reference eval batch tests policy consistency, not business impact.

title: Tool registry and structured workflow contracts
claim: Defined inspectable tools for requirement extraction, evidence lookup, proof matching, review routing, package assembly and evaluation.
evidence: Public tool registry documents inputs, outputs, side effects and approval rules.
boundary: Reference tool contracts; the evidence lookup is lexical/reference retrieval, not production RAG.

title: Prompt contracts with anti-fabrication guardrails
claim: Defined prompt contracts for requirement extraction, evidence matching, package generation and human review with explicit no-fabrication rules.
evidence: Public prompt files specify structured output, provenance checks and human-review conditions.
boundary: Prompt contracts are reference artifacts, not production prompt-performance evidence.

title: Evaluation batch for routing quality
claim: Built a reference eval batch covering direct match, adjacent evidence, overclaim prevention, human review and missing proof.
evidence: Reference eval runner compares expected vs actual routing decisions.
boundary: Small synthetic/reference batch; not statistical validation.

title: Evidence-first portfolio operating system
claim: Built a reusable method for separating verified evidence, modeled impact, ownership boundaries and missing proof across portfolio artifacts.
evidence: Current case/evidence system explicitly tracks source, confidence, responsibility boundary and gaps instead of flattening everything into marketing claims.
boundary: Method/system evidence; not a standalone commercial product yet.

title: Public/private evidence boundary
claim: Separates public-safe artifacts from interview-only and private source material.
evidence: Current evidence-pack workflow includes explicit publication boundaries and sanitization rules.
